question: Which of the following is the primary cause of the rain shadow effect in the Western Ghats region of India?

options.text: The Himalayas blocking the monsoon winds
The Western Ghats intercepting moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea
The Thar Desert drawing moisture from the monsoon winds
The Deccan Plateau blocking winds from the Bay of Bengal

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Western Ghats intercepting moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea**__.

**__Key Points__**

• The **Western Ghats**, also known as the **Sahyadri** range, act as a continuous mountain barrier along the western coast of **India**. This physical structure is the primary reason for the **rain shadow effect** observed in the interior regions of the **Deccan Plateau**.

• When the **South-West Monsoon** winds arrive from the **Arabian Sea** during the months of **June to September**, they are heavily laden with moisture. These winds strike the **windward side** (western slopes) of the **Western Ghats**, forcing the air to rise.

• As the air rises, it cools and condenses, leading to heavy **orographic rainfall** on the coastal plains and the western slopes. Some areas here receive more than **250 cm** to **400 cm** of annual rainfall. **Hence, statement 2 is correct.**
